key_insight: Changing the halide in Ca$_3$PX$_3$ strongly tunes the electronic and photovoltaic response, with iodine substitution giving the best overall solar-cell performance.
engineering_relevance: Halide engineering offers a practical design lever for optimizing perovskite absorbers for higher-efficiency optoelectronic devices.
method: First-principles structural analysis across Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I)
Electronic band-structure calculation to determine bandgap type and magnitude
SLME-based photovoltaic screening to estimate solar-cell efficiency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps spanning 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME results showing Ca$_3$PI$_3$ at 29.6% efficiency versus only 0.6% for Ca$_3$PF$_3$.
watch_item: The reported efficiencies are theoretical screening results, so experimental stability, fabrication, and device-integration effects still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
